w10_T4_003337: Jason had 240 cents saved in his piggy bank, an amount his older sister liked to point out was just under two and a half dollars. One afternoon he split the coins evenly with his younger brother so each of them would have spending money for the fair. After buying a sticker for 5 cents at the entrance booth, he wandered over to a coin-multiplier game that promised to turn every cent into eight cents, and he walked away with eight times what he'd fed into the machine. His grandmother then gave him 55 cents for helping weed her garden that morning, and his aunt slipped him another 44 cents as a birthday treat. How many cents did Jason have in the end?
w10_T4_003339: Every morning, Marcus opens his food truck's cash drawer with exactly $118 left over from the day before. By mid-morning he had taken in $80 from the breakfast crowd, even though a dozen of his regular customers paid with cards instead of cash. In the early afternoon he had to pay a produce supplier $157 for a delivery, a round trip that took 120 minutes, a full two hours, through downtown traffic. That same afternoon, a promotional partner matched whatever was left in the drawer four times over as part of a grand-opening event. By evening, Marcus split that afternoon total evenly four ways among his four business partners, keeping only his own share in the drawer. He then added $67 from the dinner rush, but had to pay out $103 to cover a broken generator. How much money was left in the drawer at closing?
w10_T4_003344: Nina counted $45 in her wallet, quite a bit more than the $10 her friend Priya had brought along, and tucked a dozen stickers into her pocket just for fun. At the farmers market she sold a hand-painted birdhouse and earned $62. She then spent $60 on a new set of paintbrushes and $5 on a lemonade to cool off. Later she paid her younger cousin $29 for helping carry supplies back to the car, and finally gave $12 to the market's donation jar for local schools. How much money did Nina have left?
w10_T4_003345: On Monday morning, a hardware store had 228 hammers in stock, though 90 of them were still shrink-wrapped from a shipment nobody had logged yet. By midday, a contractor bought 168 hammers for a big framing job. In the afternoon a supplier dropped off 25 replacement hammers, and by evening a return truck brought back another 50 that customers had exchanged. That night, the store tripled its hammer stock by unpacking cases from the back room, ending with three times as many hammers as it had before the unpacking. How many hammers did the store have after unpacking the cases?
w10_T4_003350: A video game character begins a level with 206 points. She collects a bonus chest worth 27 points, though a nearby sign boasts that 500 players have beaten this level before her. She then steps on a triple-point tile that multiplies her entire score by three. Falling into a spike trap costs her 241 points, but finishing a side quest earns her 38 points back. Finally, missing the last jump costs her 235 points. What is her score at the end of the level?
w10_T4_003354: Camila had 168 minutes of phone data left at the start of the month, just under three hours as her plan summary put it. She earned 38 bonus minutes for referring a friend, then used up 205 minutes during a long weekend of video calls with family. Her provider credited her 36 minutes back after a service outage, and separately mailed her a coupon for a dozen free stickers that had nothing to do with her data plan. Finally, she redeemed a survey reward worth 28 minutes. How many minutes did Camila have left?
w10_T4_003356: A moving company's truck started the day loaded with 209 boxes. At the first stop the crew picked up 19 more boxes, and at the second stop they added 44 boxes, even as the dispatch radio mentioned an unrelated truck across town carrying 1,200 boxes. At the third stop, they delivered 205 boxes to a client's new office. Back at the depot, seven identical truckloads arrived at the same time, so the loading dock ended up holding eight times as many boxes as this one truck alone had carried. A late vendor delivery then added 63 more boxes, and 447 boxes went out on the evening shipment to local stores. How many boxes were left at the depot?
w10_T4_003359: Farmer Diego had 183 chickens on his farm, noticeably more than the 40 chickens his neighbor Elena kept. A fox got into the coop overnight and 68 chickens went missing. The next week, Diego bought 9 more chicks from a hatchery. When breeding season hit, each hen ended up raising a brood that quadrupled the flock's size, four times what he had going into spring. Finally, he took in 5 more chickens from a retiring farmer down the road. How many chickens did Diego end up with?
w10_T4_003369: Every week, Owen drops his spare change into a savings jar; it started the month with $47 in it, or 4,700 cents as the bank's fine print liked to put it. He spent $18 on a new soccer ball, but earned $74 mowing lawns over the weekend. A neighborhood contest then quadrupled the jar's total as a prize for mowing the most lawns. Finally, he added $6 from his allowance. How many dollars are in Owen's jar now?
w10_T4_003380: When the fair opened at sunrise, the raffle booth had 24 rolls of tickets on the table, plus a dozen unrelated punch cards for the ring-toss game sitting off to the side. Three volunteers split the rolls evenly between them, and this story follows only the head volunteer's share from here on. Later that morning she printed 21 more tickets from a backup roll to replace some torn ones. By afternoon, a printer malfunction stapled six duplicate tickets to every single one she had, multiplying her stack sixfold. The booth manager then handed her 46 more tickets salvaged from a rained-out booth. That evening, a recount discovered that every ticket in her stack was actually part of a bundle of seven, multiplying her true count sevenfold, and 625 of those tickets were pulled and used for the evening's raffle drawing. How many tickets did she have left after the drawing?
w10_T4_003385: A bookstore had 170 novels on its shelves at the start of the sale, plus a dozen bookmarks that were never counted as inventory. A big shipment brought in 66 new novels the same day, but a water leak in the storeroom ruined 61 books beyond sale. A regional distributor then agreed to send seven copies for every novel that survived, multiplying the shelf count sevenfold. The store manager added 72 novels from a returned order, and a local author donated another 47 signed copies. How many novels did the bookstore have on its shelves after the donation?
w10_T4_003389: Sophie had $193 saved for a new bicycle, well ahead of her brother Max's $75. She earned $69 more doing yard work for a neighbor, then found $5 in an old coat pocket. Her grandmother mailed her $40 for her birthday, and a bank promotion doubled the balance in her savings account as a one-time bonus. How much money did Sophie have after the bonus?
w10_T4_003393: Liam had 45 marbles at the start of recess, compared to his friend Noah's dozen or so. He won 26 more marbles in a game against a classmate. Then a marble machine at the school fair multiplied his stash eightfold when he fed it in for a bonus round. He and three friends split what came out evenly, four ways, and he kept his own share. A trade with his teacher earned him 59 more marbles, but he lost 22 in a game he didn't play carefully. How many marbles did Liam end up with?
w10_T4_003394: On the morning of the science fair, Priya's petri dish held 89 bacteria cells, according to her 9 a.m. count, just three hours, or 180 minutes, before the noon judging. A contamination event that morning killed off 38 of the cells. Over the next few hours, the surviving colony multiplied sevenfold as it fed on the agar's nutrients. By afternoon, a warmer incubator setting caused the colony to multiply another fivefold. Priya then introduced 41 cells from a backup sample she'd been growing separately. By evening, a final growth spurt multiplied the whole colony sixfold before the judges scored it. How many bacteria cells were in the dish by evening?
w10_T4_003397: A factory's storage bin held 173 gears at the start of the shift, right next to a completely separate crate of 500 bolts that nobody was tracking that day. A dozen workers watched as a new machine replaced every gear with six identical replacements, sixfolding the bin's count as part of a quality-matching process. The batch was then split evenly into three shipments bound for three different plants, and only the shipment that stayed on-site is tracked from here. A supplier delivered 49 more gears to restock the bin that afternoon. Finally, a partner plant matched the bin's gear count eight times over as part of a bulk trade agreement. How many gears were in the bin after the trade?
w10_T4_003398: A packing house's bin held 240 apples at the start of the morning, though the manager mentioned a completely unrelated order of 10,000 apples destined for a different client entirely. Workers picked 20 more apples and tossed them into the same bin. To fill a large export order, the crew multiplied the bin's contents ninefold by matching every apple with eight more from cold storage. That export batch was then split evenly across five delivery trucks, and only the lead truck's load is tracked from here. The lead truck's apples were further divided evenly onto six pallets for the warehouse, and only one of those pallets continued to the final buyer. Finally, 23 apples from a late harvest were added to that pallet. How many apples were on the pallet after the late harvest was added?
w10_T4_003401: Derek owned 217 trading cards, far more than his cousin Bianca's 15. At a swap meet he traded up and gained 67 more cards. A rare booster-box promotion then let him multiply his entire collection ninefold by redeeming a golden ticket. A second, even rarer promotion at a different booth multiplied his whole collection another fourfold. Later, he sold off 367 duplicate cards to a dealer to make room in his binder. How many cards did Derek have left after the sale?
w10_T4_003403: At sunrise, a beekeeper counted 189 bees in a new hive, alongside a completely unrelated apiary a mile away that was said to hold a dozen hives of its own. By mid-morning, the queen's brood hatched, and the colony's population became four times what it had been at sunrise. In the afternoon, a spell of cold weather caused 215 bees to die off. Later that afternoon, a second wave of hatching multiplied the surviving colony sixfold. That evening, a swarm split off, taking 1,484 bees away to start a new hive elsewhere. Overnight, 27 bees returned after getting lost during the swarm. By the next morning, a pesticide drift in a nearby field killed off 572 more bees. How many bees remained in the original hive?
w10_T4_003404: In the morning, a bakery had 137 loaves of bread on the shelf. By midday, 32 loaves were sold to a catering order. In the afternoon, the bakery's ovens finished a large batch that multiplied the shelf count sevenfold to restock for the evening rush. That evening, a wedding order added 40 more loaves fresh from a partner bakery. Late that night, the overnight crew baked and added 28 more loaves for the next morning's opening. How many loaves were on the shelf by the next morning?
w10_T4_003406: On Saturday morning, Elena had 96 stamps in her album, well more than her pen pal Fatima's dozen or so loose stamps. She split her collection evenly among three trade binders that morning, and this story follows only the first binder from here. In the afternoon, a stamp-collecting club gave her 49 more stamps as a welcome gift. By evening, a trade event let her multiply that binder's stamps sixfold by swapping duplicates with other collectors. Late that night, 29 stamps turned out to be damaged and had to be discarded, and another 8 were returned to their original owner by mistake. How many stamps were in Elena's first binder after the corrections?
w10_T4_003409: A theater had 129 seats reserved for a school trip, while a completely unrelated concert next door had booked 500 seats of its own. A dozen chaperones came along, though that number played no role in the seat count as 43 students had to cancel due to a scheduling conflict. Afterward, 36 more students from another class joined the trip. Then 92 seats were released back to the box office when a different school pulled out of a joint booking. Finally, 30 walk-up students joined, and 78 more students from a nearby school added their names to the trip. How many students ended up going on the trip?
w10_T4_003423: Maria's savings account held 201 dollars, or 20,100 cents as the bank teller once pointed out. She deposited 42 dollars from her paycheck, along with a loyalty card now stamped a dozen times, which earned her no extra cash. A loyalty bonus then multiplied her balance sevenfold as a reward for years of banking with them. She split that reward evenly three ways with her two siblings, keeping only her own third. Finally, she paid 542 dollars toward a new laptop. How much money did Maria have left in her account?
w10_T4_003425: Tariq had 70 tokens at the arcade, more than his friend Sam's 15. He spent 47 tokens on a racing game. He then spent 21 more tokens on skee-ball. A prize booth then multiplied his remaining tokens fourfold as a special promotion for the last hour. Finally, he spent 6 tokens on a claw machine. How many tokens did Tariq have left?
w10_T4_003426: In the morning, a food bank had 152 canned goods on its shelves, along with a dozen volunteers ready to help sort donations. By midday, a local grocery store donated 65 more cans, even though a news report mentioned a different food bank across town receiving 900 cans that day. In the afternoon, a school food drive added 4 more cans. By evening, a church group brought in 54 additional cans. Late that night, volunteers packed and distributed 168 cans to families in need. How many canned goods were left on the shelves after the distribution?
w10_T4_003428: Jake had 214 baseball cards, more than his friend Marcus's 90. A trading event doubled his entire collection when he matched every card with an identical one from a bulk lot. He then found 4 more cards under his bed. He split the collection evenly among six binders, keeping only one binder's worth. That binder was further divided evenly across four subject dividers, and he kept only the modern-era divider's cards. Finally, he bought 19 more modern-era cards at a shop. How many cards were in that divider afterward?
